:::{#thm-cosine-bijection}
#### Cosine takes each value from $-1$ to $1$ exactly once between $0$ and $\pi$

The function $\cos : [0, \pi] \to [-1, 1]$ is decreasing, with $\cos 0 = 1$ and $\cos\pi = -1$,
and takes each value in $[-1, 1]$ exactly once.
On $[0, \pi]$, $\sin\angpar \ge 0$.

:::

::: proof

For $\angpar \in [0, \pi]$, the point $(\cos\angpar, \sin\angpar)$ is at distance $\angpar$ along the circle
from $(1, 0)$, counterclockwise, so it lies on the upper half of the unit circle,
$\set{(x_1, x_2) : x_1^2 + x_2^2 = 1,\ x_2 \ge 0}$, which gives $\sin\angpar \ge 0$.
Different values of $\angpar$ in $[0, \pi]$ are different distances along that half circle,
so they give different points.
Two different points of the upper half have different first coordinates,
because $x_2 = \sqrt{1 - x_1^2}$ is determined by $x_1$.
So $\cos$ is one-to-one on $[0, \pi]$.
Every $x_1 \in [-1, 1]$ is the first coordinate of the point $(x_1, \sqrt{1 - x_1^2})$ of the upper half,
and the distance along the half circle from $(1, 0)$ to that point is some $\angpar \in [0, \pi]$,
so $\cos$ takes every value in $[-1, 1]$.
A one-to-one continuous function that goes from $1$ at $0$ to $-1$ at $\pi$ is decreasing.

:::
